title: Accelerating an overhead-sensitive atmospheric model on GPUs using asynchronous execution and kernel fusion
problem: Kernel launch overhead significantly limits GPU performance for atmospheric models, causing default synchronous execution on A100 GPUs to underperform A64FX CPUs in strong scaling.
motivation: Mitigating kernel launch overhead is essential for enabling GPUs to efficiently run overhead-sensitive atmospheric models and maintain competitiveness with CPU implementations.
method: OpenACC is used to enable asynchronous kernel execution across single or multiple GPU queues, reducing synchronization overhead. CUDA kernel fusion collocates multiple loops within a single kernel using block-index-based branching to further reduce kernel launch counts.
key_novelty: Systematic application of both OpenACC asynchronous execution and CUDA kernel fusion to eliminate kernel launch overhead in atmospheric models, achieving significant combined speedup.
contributions: Single-queue asynchronous execution implementation using OpenACC achieving 37% runtime reduction
CUDA kernel fusion approach combining loop operations through block-based branching for additional 10% acceleration
Demonstration that single-queue asynchronous execution is more practical than multi-queue approaches for overhead-sensitive workloads
Performance comparison against A64FX CPU establishing GPU competitiveness with overhead mitigation techniques

metrics.speedup: 37% runtime reduction with single-queue asynchronous execution; additional 10% with kernel fusion

limitations: Trade-offs between OpenACC portability and CUDA kernel fusion effectiveness, and potential benefits of CUDA Graphs for frequently executed kernels, are mentioned but not thoroughly analyzed.
primary_theme: Kernel launch overhead reduction for GPU-accelerated atmospheric models
